source.title: A Bayesian Perspective on the Role of Epistemic Uncertainty for Delayed Generalization in In-Context Learning

page_placements.theme: Entropy, information and uncertainty around the transition

record.tranche_reason: It investigates delayed generalization in modular arithmetic in-context learning, using Bayesian uncertainty measures and a simplified linear model rather than reproducing the original grokking method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an optimization-time accuracy and epistemic-uncertainty trajectory for a transformer (Figure 7), and theoretical results on delayed generalization and uncertainty peaks in a simplified Bayesian linear model. The accuracy heatmaps across task counts and training-data fractions, and the context-length and context-noise plots, do not report optimization-time grokking outcomes, so they are not separate rows. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper takes grokking in modular-linear ICL (from He et al. 2024) as given and studies epistemic uncertainty (EU) as a label-free diagnostic of it. Its one optimization-time trajectory (Fig. 7) shows OOD Val accuracy and EU only. It reports no training accuracy, so the gap after training saturation cannot be read. Nothing tracks circuits, memorization removal, data-size scaling of the delay, optimizer artifacts or regime switches. The theory is Bayesian linear regression following Levi et al. (2024), not an algorithmic dataset or circuit. The main measured quantity, EU, is a confidence score rather than the behaviour or its mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that EU collapses sharply at grokking in a modular linear ICL setting, giving a label-free diagnostic. The signal is robust across IVON and Last-Layer Laplace and remains informative under changes in task diversity, context length and context noise. A simplified Bayesian linear model shows delayed generalization and EU peaks share a spectral mechanism. They caution that the setting is synthetic and that extending to larger models needs care. Note that the EU peak precedes, rather than coincides with, the accuracy threshold.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses modular linear in-context learning tasks and measures Bayesian predictive uncertainty with IVON and Last-Layer Laplace, alongside a simplified Bayesian linear-model analysis, rather than reproducing the original grokking training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: OOD Val generalization varies with task count, training-data fraction, and inference method: Laplace generalizes across more configurations, while IVON is competitive mainly at the highest training-data fractions. Context length and context noise also change accuracy and uncertainty, but these are not optimization-time grokking tests.

fits_no_version.finding: In the full transformer (Fig. 7), the EU peak on OOD Val occurs before OOD Val accuracy crosses its threshold. EU then collapses as accuracy rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epistemic uncertainty rises and then collapses around the grokking transition, providing a label-free signal that precedes the accuracy threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the endpoint grid (Fig. 3), EU drops sharply at T=256 and T=512 tasks for both IVON and Laplace, matching where OOD generalization appears.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-checkpoint epistemic uncertainty tracks whether ICL task generalization has been reached as task diversity grows.

fits_no_version.finding: In Bayesian linear regression under Gaussian VI, the train–generalization delays in the accuracy threshold and in the EU peak both grow as λ=d/n→1. Both are attributed to the lower Marchenko–Pastur edge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In linear-Gaussian models, delayed generalization and delayed uncertainty peaks share a spectral-edge origin, with delay ∝ log(1/(1−√λ)).

record.problems: The full-transformer temporal trajectory is presented as a figure without numerical values, and the accompanying text does not establish the training-accuracy saturation or smaller-training-set delay components of V1. The theoretical delay result is for a simplified model. The authors also identify the empirical work as a specific synthetic setting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted. The endpoint heatmaps and context-length/context-noise measurements are not optimization-time delayed-generalization results; cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation preceding the test jump, and growth of the delay as the training set shrinks. The α sweep reports endpoint accuracy only, not grokking time.
Gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, and circuit-level progress measures.
Non-algorithmic data; initialization-scale or weight-norm switching.
Efficiency account, critical dataset size, ungrokking. Weight decay is used but not varied.
Optimizer or numerical artifact controls. AdamW and IVON are both used but not compared on grokking delay.

missing.what: Endpoint OOD Train and OOD Val accuracy across task count T and training fraction α for IVON vs Laplace. Generalization appears only at T≥256, and IVON needs high α. These are not grokking-time results but bear on the conditions for generalization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' labels for V1 and V2 are removed. The V1 trajectory lacks training accuracy, so it cannot show delayed generalization. V2's link rested on treating an uncertainty score as a mechanism measure. The grokking behaviour itself was established by He et al. (2024); this paper's contribution is the uncertainty diagnostic.

versions.untested_parts: The reported transformer trajectory does not establish that training accuracy has saturated while test accuracy remains at chance, nor test how the optimization delay changes as the training set shrinks.

The study measures epistemic uncertainty around generalization, but does not track formation of a Fourier or other identifiable generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or continuous circuit-level progress.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule training setting, nor initialization-scale or weight-norm transition, is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
Weight decay is used in training, but the proposed efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking are not tested.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test whether grokking is an optimizer or numerical artifact, or whether it disappears when such choices are controlled.

relation.reason: Grokking supplies the setting for evaluating an uncertainty diagnostic, but the reported results do not establish the behavior or mechanism specified by any claim version.

tranche.reason: The paper studies uncertainty as a diagnostic of presumed grokking. Its transformer trajectory reports OOD validation accuracy and uncertainty without training-accuracy saturation or a dataset-size-dependent delay; its linear-model theory does not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Both delays have leading asymptotic form log(1/(1−√λ))/[(n/σ²)(1−√λ)²+1/τ²]. The uncertainty result concerns thresholded-success entropy, assumes late-time peaks, and allows subleading corrections; it does not identify a generalizing circuit.
